items.title: Velocita 1.0 is here
items.summary: Starter templates, one-command deploys, a performance budget and a Lighthouse CI gate. Here is what shipped in 1.0.
items.content_html:
What's new

Velocita 1.0 completes the road from "fast by default" to "stays fast in production":

  • Starter templates for a blog, docs and a local business, each scoring Lighthouse 100 in every category
  • velocita deploy for Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel and GitHub Pages
  • velocita check, a browser-free performance budget that runs in milliseconds
  • A Lighthouse CI gate written for you, failing CI below 95

Why a budget matters

Sites rarely start slow; they get slow one dependency at a time. A budget that runs on every build turns "we should keep it fast" into a failing check. Read more in why zero JavaScript is a feature.

Get it

Follow Getting started, or pick a template.

items.title: A practical guide to llms.txt and AI search
items.summary: What llms.txt is, what it is not, and the other signals that help AI answer engines read and cite your content.
items.content_html:
What llms.txt is

llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file at the root of a site that lists its most useful pages with short descriptions, so language models can find clean content quickly. Velocita writes it, plus llms-full.txt with the full text, on every build.

What it is not

It is not a ranking factor for Google, and AI crawlers are not required to read it. Treat it as a cheap, helpful extra, not a strategy.

Signals that matter more

  • Clean, crawlable HTML with real headings, which every page already has
  • Markdown copies of each page, such as this one, for agents that prefer text
  • Structured data that states facts explicitly
  • A clear crawler policy with aiCrawlers: 'allow' | 'search-only' | 'block'

See the full list in SEO and AI search, or read why zero JavaScript is a feature.

items.title: Why zero JavaScript is a feature
items.summary: Content sites rarely need a client-side framework. Here is what shipping no JS by default buys you, and how to add interactivity anyway.
items.content_html:
The cost you don't see

Every kilobyte of JavaScript is downloaded, parsed, compiled and executed before a page becomes fully responsive. On a mid-range phone that cost shows up directly in Interaction to Next Paint.

What content sites actually need

Most pages of a blog, docs site or marketing site are text, images and links. HTML already does that perfectly. The few interactive parts, such as search, a copy button or a calculator, can be islands that load on their own.

Measuring it

The home page runs a live meter that shows its own transfer size, JavaScript weight and Largest Contentful Paint in your browser. Then try the 1.0 release notes to see what keeps those numbers low over time.
